shared: The Karhu was introduced in 3079 as the first Clan-technology OmniMech produced by Odin Manufacturing for the Ghost Bear Dominion. Named after the Finnish word for "bear," the sixty-five-ton heavy OmniMech was designed to fill the Dominion's need for a fast cavalry platform built with the latest Clan technology. Odin Manufacturing, based on the former Free Rasalhague Republic world of Orestes, won a competitive contract against their chief rival Bergan Industries in 3077, delivering a design that earned a fierce reputation as a frontline cavalry 'Mech despite lingering questions about its electronics reliability. The Karhu remains a symbol of the Dominion's industrial ambitions and a mainstay of its frontline clusters.

The Karhu is built around a Beowulf 4 Enhanced endo steel chassis powered by a Pitban 325-rated extra-light engine, giving the sixty-five-ton OmniMech a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. Ten and a half tons of Compound A2F ferro-fibrous armor provide solid protection for its weight class, while twelve fixed double heat sinks manage baseline waste heat across its varied configurations. This combination of speed, protection, and Clan-grade construction leaves an impressive thirty tons of available pod space for mission-specific equipment.

The Prime configuration reflects the design's appeal to the KungsArmé tradition of physical combat, mounting a retractable blade sculpted into a fearsome three-pronged claw alongside a plasma cannon in the right arm. An ER PPC and ER medium laser in the left arm provide ranged firepower, while improved jump jets grant exceptional battlefield mobility. However, Odin's relative inexperience with Clan technology has manifested in documented electronics reliability issues. The firm reused the Beowulf's proven Dash-2 Standard communications system and Blade 12 targeting computer to save development time, but intermittent compatibility glitches with Clan-manufactured components have plagued the design in the field, a problem technicians attribute to fundamental incompatibilities between Inner Sphere electronics architectures and Clan equipment.

The Karhu's development was born from the merger of the Free Rasalhague Republic and the Ghost Bear Dominion, which opened Clan technology to Inner Sphere manufacturers for the first time. For Odin Manufacturing, the merger represented both opportunity and challenge. Their Orestes production facility had been damaged by Word of Blake raids in the late 3060s, and the demands of the Jihad forced them to continue producing existing Inner Sphere designs while simultaneously planning their transition to Clan-technology manufacturing. By 3077, when the Dominion announced a competition for a new heavy OmniMech, Odin was finally ready to make the leap.

The competition between Odin and their rival Bergan Industries proved fierce. Odin identified Bergan as their primary competitor and designed the Karhu specifically to outperform whatever Bergan produced, while simultaneously launching a marketing campaign rooted in Rasalhagian nationalism aimed at former KungsArme officers within the Dominion touman. This strategy proved effective, and Odin won the contract in 3079 with a design that was widely acknowledged as technologically superior to Bergan's competing entry, the Arcas.

First deployed in 3079, the Karhu arrived too late to participate in Operation SCOUR but rapidly became a fixture in the Dominion's frontline clusters. Paired frequently with the Ursus II, the Karhu earned a reputation as a cavalry 'Mech, flanking opponents while heavier designs drew fire at close range. During the Jihad's final stages and the early Republic era, Karhus were concentrated in frontline formations alongside Vultures and other OmniMechs, forming the mobile striking arm of Dominion combined-arms doctrine.

The design's success has not been without controversy. Competition between Odin and Bergan Industries has grown increasingly bitter, with Odin officials publicly disparaging Bergan as "that Capellan company with their Combine workers." Requests for Orestes-built 'Mechs are noticeably higher among Rasalhagian warriors as a result of this rivalry. The Ghost Bear Council has expressed concern over this infighting and has requested that representatives of both companies exercise restraint, though reports suggest the merchants are too deeply engaged in their competition to easily comply.

The Karhu's documented electronics reliability issues have been a persistent concern throughout its service history. Technicians have traced the intermittent glitches to fundamental incompatibilities between the Inner Sphere-designed communications and targeting systems and the Clan-manufactured components they interface with, citing similar problems on Beowulfs retrofitted with Clan equipment. Odin has denied culpability, but the issue remains unresolved and represents an ongoing maintenance burden for Dominion technicians. Despite this flaw, the Karhu's combination of speed, firepower, and pod flexibility has ensured its continued prominence in the Dominion's order of battle, with the 2nd Legion of Vega's attack on the Orestes production line in 3099 emphasizing both the design's strategic importance and its vulnerability to disruption.

shared:
The Kit Fox was introduced in 2890 by Clan Cloud Cobra, the first product of newly acquired resources from the Tanite Worlds. Designated the Uller by Inner Sphere forces after the Norse god of archery, the Kit Fox was designed as a heavily armed light OmniMech that prioritized firepower and protection over raw speed. This philosophy placed it in deliberate contrast to the Fire Moth, offering Clan commanders a complementary light chassis capable of engaging heavier opponents at range rather than relying on speed for survival.

The Kit Fox quickly proved its worth in combat, and Clan Jade Falcon secured production rights through a narrowly won Trial of Possession against the Cloud Cobras. Clan Snow Raven acquired manufacturing rights through trade, while Clan Blood Spirit received the design as a gift from the Ravens. All other Clans field the Kit Fox as isorla, making it one of the most widespread light OmniMechs in Clan service. The Jade Falcons became so closely associated with the design that a Clan Coyote adage warns warriors to double their caution when encountering a Falcon pilot outside a Summoner, Hellbringer, or Kit Fox.

The Kit Fox chassis mounts a Starfire 180 XL engine, providing a top speed of just over ninety-seven kilometers per hour. While this makes it one of the slower light OmniMechs in Clan inventories, the weight savings from the extralight engine, Process 12 endo-steel internal structure, and four tons of Compound H18 ferro-fibrous armor free an impressive sixteen tons of pod space. This generous payload capacity allows the Kit Fox to mount weapon loadouts rivaling many medium-weight designs, and ten fixed double heat sinks provide a solid thermal management foundation for energy-intensive configurations.

In its Primary configuration, the Kit Fox carries an ER large laser and small pulse laser in the left arm alongside an LB 5-X autocannon and Streak SRM-4 launcher in the right arm. This combination provides effective engagement capability from long range down to close quarters, with the LB-X offering tactical flexibility through its cluster and slug ammunition options. The design earns its archery-themed codename through configurations that consistently emphasize ranged precision over close-quarters brawling.

The Kit Fox suffers from its relatively low speed and lack of jump capability on the base chassis, and MechWarriors who allow faster opponents to close range can find themselves outmaneuvered despite superior firepower. The narrow, low-profile frame provides some compensation, making the Kit Fox a more difficult target than its tonnage might suggest.

The Kit Fox emerged during a period of expansion for Clan Cloud Cobra, as newly secured resources from the Tanite Worlds enabled ambitious weapons development programs. First produced in 2890, the design saw immediate success in the Fang Clusters, where Cloud Cobra forces employed Kit Foxes to devastating effect against Clan Jade Falcon and Clan Coyote opponents. The string of Cloud Cobra victories attracted the attention of Jade Falcon Khan Bret Malthus, who issued a formal challenge for possession of the design. The resulting Trial was fought on the desolate wastelands of Babylon, where the Jade Falcons secured victory by the narrowest of margins.

Under Jade Falcon stewardship, the Kit Fox became a mainstay of the Clan's light second-line forces. Clan Snow Raven acquired manufacturing rights through trade rather than combat, choosing commerce over conflict as a means of securing the design. The Ravens subsequently gifted the Kit Fox to Clan Blood Spirit, an act viewed by some observers as either genuine generosity or a calculated political maneuver. All other Clans that field the Kit Fox do so through battlefield salvage, ensuring a broad but uneven distribution across Clan space.

During Operation Revival, the Kit Fox proved a nasty surprise for Inner Sphere forces who underestimated the small OmniMech. Configuration A's Gauss rifle was particularly shocking to Inner Sphere commanders, who did not expect such devastating firepower from a light chassis. The Federated Commonwealth was sufficiently impressed to commission the Hollander, a dedicated light Gauss rifle platform inspired by the Kit Fox A. Inner Sphere intelligence designated the OmniMech the Uller, and it quickly became one of the most recognized Clan designs among Spheroid military analysts.

In the Raven Alliance, the Kit Fox found renewed production at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Beta on Mitchella, supplementing the traditional Clan homeworld factories. The 100th Raven Battle Cluster especially employed Kit Foxes configured for mobile artillery support during the seizure of Inner End from the Federated Suns in 3144, where the OmniMechs obliterated fixed anti-aircraft defenses and cleared the path for aerospace fighter strikes. Earlier, Kit Fox-anchored scout Stars had played a central role in destroying elements of the Third Crucis Lancers on Tellman IV in 3072, actions later dramatized in numerous books and holovids across Raven Alliance space.

Production of the Kit Fox has continued across multiple eras, with new configurations appearing to incorporate advancing weapons technology. Eagle Craft Group maintained Jade Falcon production on Erewhon until approximately 3070, when the line was shuttered as newer designs like the Hierofalcon and Ion Sparrow entered service. Mobile factory ships continued Kit Fox production for the Jade Falcons, ensuring the design remained available even as permanent facilities shifted to other chassis. The Kit Fox remains less common among Clans that must rely solely on battlefield captures, though those that do field it continue to value the design's combination of pod flexibility and surprising durability.

shared: The Linebacker was commissioned in 3052 by Clan Wolf Khans to address a critical gap in their heavy OmniMech roster. The venerable Timber Wolf, while devastating in stand-up engagements, struggled to keep pace with lighter Star-mates during running battles, limiting the tactical flexibility of front-line Clusters. Designed to pair the firepower expected of a sixty-five-ton OmniMech with the speed of designs ten tons lighter, the Linebacker was intended to supplement and eventually replace the Timber Wolf in Wolf offensive formations. Its distinctive hunched profile, said to resemble the players of ancient Terran American Football, earned it the codename that became its official designation. Though its Warden origins initially limited acceptance among Crusader Wolves, the Linebacker has proven itself across multiple theaters and Clans, establishing a reputation as one of the fastest heavy OmniMechs in production.

The Linebacker achieves its remarkable speed through a Heavy Force 390-rated XL engine, propelling the sixty-five-ton OmniMech to a top speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour. This engine choice is the defining trade-off of the design, consuming significant mass that would otherwise be available for weapons and equipment. The result is 17.5 tons of pod space, roughly ten tons less than the Timber Wolf it was designed to complement. The Type W4 Endo Steel frame provides structural savings, while ten tons of Composite A-4 ferro-fibrous armor delivers respectable protection for a 'Mech expected to operate at the leading edge of an advance.

In its primary configuration, the Linebacker mounts a pair of ER PPCs that deliver devastating firepower at extreme range, backed by an LRM-5 launcher for supplementary bombardment. A Streak SRM-4 provides efficient close-range punch, while a rear-mounted ER Small Laser discourages pursuit. This loadout allows the Linebacker to engage effectively while maintaining the speed to choose its engagements. The low-slung, hunched torso profile provides an exceptionally stable firing platform, enabling accurate fire even at high speeds. Common configurations either exploit the Linebacker's speed to maintain standoff range while sniping, or leverage that same velocity to rapidly close distance and overwhelm enemy positions.

The Linebacker was born from battlefield necessity during the Clan Invasion. Commissioned by Khans Ward and Kerensky in 3052, the design entered production at Wolf Clan Site 2 on Strana Mechty and WC Site 1 on Arc-Royal. A Trinary formed from the first production run deployed to Tukayyid with Gamma Galaxy, where the Linebacker saw its baptism of fire against ComStar defenders. Though the design performed admirably, the upheaval of the Refusal War and the Crusader Wolves' disdain for what they viewed as a Warden creation prevented the Linebacker from appearing in significant numbers until the mid-3060s.

Before the Refusal War, the Wolves had shared the Linebacker design with Clans Snow Raven and Coyote. As Wolf combat losses mounted in the years that followed, the design spread further through Clan politics and warfare. Clan Hell's Horses and the Jade Falcons acquired Linebackers through various means, while fighting on Lum allowed the Steel Vipers to seize several examples, many of which later fell to the Cloud Cobras following the Viper absorption on Homer.

Clan Wolf proper did not replace Linebackers lost during the Jihad, and the design became a common sight only among the Wolves-in-Exile, who maintained constant production at their Arc-Royal facilities. The loss of Arc-Royal to the Jade Falcons forced the Exiles to scramble, eventually relocating production to fall-back facilities on Donegal under the Assault Tech Industries banner.

The Linebacker experienced a dramatic resurgence when Khan Alaric Ward ordered the design back into mass production for the Wolf Empire. W-12 Facilities on Zosma joined the production effort as the Linebacker was recast as a mainstay of the Wolf Empire's heavy BattleMech forces, serving alongside the Timber Wolf, Warwolf, and Crossbow as the spearpoint of the Empire's advance toward Terra. During the conquest of the Republic Remnant, Linebackers of the 103rd Wolf Guard Striker Cluster played a decisive role in the May 3149 Battle of Alhena, where their superior speed allowed them to outflank Republic artillery positions and overrun defensive emplacements that had stalled a conventional assault.

text.deployment: A custom configuration assembled from necessity rather than design, this variant was created after a heavily damaged Karhu was salvaged following the death of its original pilot in 3085. While the Clan-technology base chassis was maintained, the replacement OmniPods use exclusively Inner Sphere components. A retractable blade and Inner Sphere plasma rifle occupy the right arm, while a heavy PPC and standard-grade ER medium laser fill the left arm. Two tons of plasma rifle ammunition provide adequate endurance. The configuration also mounts a Beagle active probe, Guardian ECM suite, and C3 slave unit, integrating it into Inner Sphere command networks and giving it respectable electronic warfare capability despite its mixed-technology nature. The use of IS-grade components results in a significantly lower combat effectiveness compared to standard configurations, but the C3 integration makes this variant valuable as part of a coordinated lance.

Configured for longer-range engagement profiles, the A configuration mounts a Gauss rifle in the right arm supported by a left-torso LRM-10, giving the Karhu credible standoff firepower. The addition of a large pulse laser, ER medium laser, and micro pulse laser in the right arm ensures the configuration remains dangerous at close range should an enemy close the distance. Two tons of Gauss ammunition and one ton of missile reloads provide reasonable endurance for sustained operations, while five standard jump jets maintain the mobility expected of the chassis. The A configuration sees frequent deployment in mixed formations where its combination of precision long-range fire and jump capability allows it to anchor defensive positions while retaining the ability to reposition quickly.

A dedicated short-range brawler, the B configuration leverages the Karhu's mobility to devastating effect by mounting a massive Ultra AC/20 in the left arm. Three ER medium lasers in the right arm supplement the autocannon's fearsome close-range damage output, while a targeting computer enhances accuracy across all weapons. Four tons of autocannon ammunition provide adequate endurance for intense engagements, and jump jets allow the configuration to navigate urban terrain and exploit cover. The addition of an ECM suite provides electronic warfare capability, making the B configuration a particularly deadly city fighter. Two additional double heat sinks help manage the thermal load generated by sustained fire from the autocannon and laser battery.

The C configuration offers a balanced mixed-range loadout, mounting dual Ultra AC/5 autocannons split between the side torsos for sustained suppressive fire at medium to long range. An ER large laser and ER medium laser in the left arm provide energy-based firepower that complements the autocannons without ammunition dependency, while a retractable blade in the right arm maintains the Karhu's characteristic close-combat capability. Each autocannon carries a ton of ammunition, and jump jets preserve the design's trademark mobility. The C configuration's versatile weapon mix makes it well-suited for extended patrol and garrison duties where ammunition resupply may be limited.

The D configuration represents the Karhu's most electronics-intensive loadout, built around a pair of ER PPCs in the left arm supported by three ER medium lasers in the right arm and a Streak SRM-6 in the left torso. A comprehensive electronics suite including a targeting computer, active probe, and ECM suite transforms the configuration into a potent command and reconnaissance platform. Dual anti-missile systems provide active defenses against incoming missiles, while four additional double heat sinks manage the substantial thermal output of the twin PPCs. With the highest operational cost among standard configurations, the D stands as a significant investment but delivers exceptional capability for independent operations and deep raids where its combination of firepower, electronic warfare, and active defenses allows it to operate effectively without support.

Developed in 3099, the G configuration introduces a supercharger that pushes the Karhu's top speed to one hundred kilometers per hour, making it one of the fastest heavy OmniMechs in the Dominion's arsenal. A one-hundred-fifty-meter jump capability further enhances its ability to evade return fire and control engagement ranges. The primary weapon is an improved heavy large laser, supported by three ER medium lasers and four Streak SRM-4 launchers that provide devastating close-range salvos. A light TAG system allows the G configuration to designate targets for artillery and semi-guided munitions, expanding its role beyond direct combat into fire support coordination. The G configuration reflects a post-Jihad design philosophy emphasizing speed and flexibility over raw firepower.

First deployed in 3079, this variant configuration arrived too late to participate in Operation SCOUR but quickly established itself as a cavalry 'Mech in the Dominion's post-Jihad touman. The combination of a retractable blade and plasma cannon appeals to warriors who favor close-quarters combat, while the ER PPC provides effective fire at longer ranges. Improved jump jets grant this variant configuration outstanding maneuverability for a heavy OmniMech, allowing it to exploit terrain and close rapidly with opponents. The design's skull-like chassis sculpting and oversized right-hand claw serve both as functional weapons and as deliberate psychological warfare tools intended to inspire fear, a quality that resonates with the Dominion's increasingly assertive military posture.

text.overview:
The King Crab was designed in 2741 by Cosara Weaponries at the direct request of General Aleksandr Kerensky for an assault 'Mech capable of crippling or destroying another BattleMech in a single salvo. Filling the role of a devastating close-range combatant, the hundred-ton King Crab earned its fearsome reputation through the raw destructive power of its twin super-heavy autocannons, mounted in distinctive claw-like arm housings that gave the design its name. Though initially envisioned as a potential command vehicle, the King Crab proved less suited to that capacity than expected, a role ultimately filled by the Atlas.

Production was centered at Cosara facilities on Mars and Northwind under Star League authority, with the design seeing widespread service in the SLDF. The devastation of the Succession Wars reduced the King Crab to near-extinction, but ComStar's secret preservation of the Mars factory ensured the design's survival and eventual return to mass production in the thirty-first century.
text.capabilities:
The King Crab's tactical doctrine is straightforward: close with the enemy and deliver overwhelming firepower. Its primary armament of twin Deathgiver Autocannon/20s represents one of the most destructive weapon pairings ever mounted on a BattleMech, capable of stripping the armor from virtually any opponent in a few devastating salvos. The autocannons are housed within reinforced arm assemblies fitted with simple hand actuators that function as protective cowlings, giving the 'Mech its distinctive crab-like silhouette and the appearance of pincers opening and closing in combat. A Simpson-15 LRM launcher and Exostar large laser provide secondary fire support at longer ranges, ensuring the King Crab is not entirely helpless during its approach to engagement range.

Sixteen tons of Aldis X ferro-fibrous armor provide solid, evenly distributed protection across the chassis, with CASE safeguarding the ammunition stores from catastrophic detonation. The arms represent a notable vulnerability, however, as an internal hit to either limb can knock an autocannon out of the fight entirely. The King Crab's most significant limitation is its dependence on ammunition; each autocannon draws from a mere five-round magazine, giving pilots limited sustained firepower before running dry. Combined with a modest top speed of 54 kilometers per hour and a well-earned reputation as a maintenance-intensive design, the King Crab demands careful tactical employment and reliable logistics to realize its devastating potential.
text.deployment: Introduced in 3143 as a factory-produced version of a successful field modification, this variant replaces the standard KGC-009's autocannons and missile launchers with Clan-specification Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifles, dramatically increasing ranged firepower. The medium lasers give way to Clan-grade ER small lasers, while Clan plasma rifles replace the Inner Sphere models for improved performance. Produced by StarCorps Industries at Loburg, this hybrid design demonstrates the increasing availability of Clan technology to Inner Sphere manufacturers during the Dark Age period, offering Lyran forces a significant upgrade in striking power while retaining the KGC-009's robust chassis and heavy armor protection.
text.battleHistory:
The King Crab's origins trace to 2741, when General Aleksandr Kerensky personally commissioned Cosara Weaponries to design an assault 'Mech of unmatched destructive power. The resulting design exceeded expectations, and production commenced at Cosara's facilities on Mars and Northwind. The King Crab served with distinction in the SLDF throughout the final decades of the Star League, though it never displaced the Atlas as the preferred command vehicle for senior officers. When the Amaris Civil War erupted in 2767, Republican forces destroyed the Mars factory, leaving only the Northwind facility operational.

The Exodus of 2784 dealt the King Crab a severe blow, as General Kerensky's departing forces took the vast majority of existing King Crabs with them, including the entire production run of the prototype KGC-010. The Northwind factory's destruction in 2786, an early casualty of the First Succession War, effectively ended new production in the Inner Sphere. The King Crab's relatively simple construction meant surviving examples were easier to maintain than many Star League-era designs, but attrition took its toll. By the close of the Third Succession War, only a handful remained in active service with the Great Houses, each one a prized and jealously guarded asset.

ComStar's seizure of Terra through Operation Silver Shield proved critical to the King Crab's survival. The order's technicians repaired and mothballed the damaged Mars factory, secretly stockpiling King Crabs for future use. By the early thirty-first century, ComStar contracted Cosara Weaponries to quietly resume production to replenish their aging reserves, equipping the Com Guards with refurbished and newly built King Crabs. The looming threat of the Clan Invasion spurred the development of the KGC-001 "Clanbuster" variant in 3052, which proved so successful at the Battle of Tukayyid that ComStar authorized general market sales from both the Mars and Northwind plants, with Cosara receiving a share of profits.

The Word of Blake's conquest of Terra and subsequent seizure of the Northwind factory in 3069 upended King Crab production once again. The Blakists retooled the Northwind line to produce their own variants, including the jump-capable KGC-008 for Protectorate forces. ComStar responded with an uncharacteristically bold move, dispatching a mercenary espionage team to infiltrate the Northwind facility and steal the new design specifications. These plans were then offered to StarCorps Industries, who eagerly began producing the KGC-007 at their Son Hoa plant for ComStar, the Lyran Alliance, and the Federated Suns alike.

The post-Jihad era saw continued evolution of the King Crab. StarCorps relocated their production line from Son Hoa to Loburg in the late 3090s, introducing the modernized KGC-009 in 3104 to meet the demands of the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces. The design proved popular with senior Lyran officers despite its continued ammunition dependency. Cosara Weaponries eventually returned the Mars facility to active production under Republic of the Sphere oversight, developing the KGC-011 with its revolutionary XXL engine for dramatically improved battlefield mobility. By the ilClan era, the King Crab remained a respected and feared assault platform, its production split between Cosara's historic Mars facility and StarCorps' Loburg plant, ensuring the design's continued presence on battlefields across the Inner Sphere.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A mounts a Gauss rifle as its primary weapon, an audacious choice for a thirty-ton OmniMech that stunned Inner Sphere forces during the Clan Invasion. Two ER medium lasers provide supporting fire at shorter ranges. The ability to deliver Gauss-level damage from a light, low-profile platform made the Kit Fox A one of the most feared configurations, directly inspiring the Federated Commonwealth's development of the Hollander BattleMech as a domestic counterpart.

Alternate Configuration B carries an Ultra AC/10 as its primary armament, a startling amount of ballistic firepower for such a small chassis. An ER medium laser, ER small laser, and SRM-6 rack provide close-range backup to finish off targets that survive the autocannon barrage. The configuration demands aggressive positioning from its pilot, as the Ultra autocannon's optimal engagement range requires closing to distances where the Kit Fox's light armor becomes a significant liability.

This variant configuration is a custom loadout developed for the Blessed Order's revived First Division, specifically the Unending Faith III. Based on the standard B configuration, this variant replaces the SRM-6 rack with an improved C3 computer, enabling network-linked targeting data sharing with compatible units. This modification sacrifices close-range missile firepower in favor of dramatically improved coordination within mixed formations, reflecting the Blessed Order's doctrinal emphasis on integrated unit tactics over individual combat prowess.

Alternate Configuration E appeared during the Civil War era, incorporating the Advanced Tactical Missile system in an ATM-3 rack that can optimize its warheads for specific engagement ranges. An ER PPC provides heavy long-range firepower, while an ER small laser handles point defense. Six jump jets grant the Kit Fox E a jump capability of one hundred eighty meters, dramatically improving its tactical mobility and allowing pilots to exploit the ATM system's range-dependent ammunition to maximum effect. The addition of jump capability addresses one of the base chassis's most significant tactical limitations.

Alternate Configuration F mounts a Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle 20, delivering enormous burst damage from a light OmniMech platform. Two medium pulse lasers provide close-range backup. The HAG system's ability to saturate a target area with multiple projectiles per volley makes the Kit Fox F particularly dangerous to light and medium targets, though ammunition constraints require pilots to choose their engagements carefully. This Jihad-era configuration reflects continuing efforts to maximize the Kit Fox's damage potential.

Alternate Configuration G pairs twin LRM-10 launchers with an ER large laser and ER medium laser in the right arm, creating a balanced fire support platform. An ECM suite in the left arm disrupts enemy targeting systems and provides electronic cover for the Kit Fox and nearby allied units. The combination of missile and energy weapons ensures the Kit Fox G can sustain fire even when ammunition runs low, while the ECM coverage makes it a valuable addition to any reconnaissance or screening force.

Alternate Configuration H appeared during the Civil War era alongside new heavy laser technology. Dual heavy medium lasers provide devastating close-range firepower, backed by a Gauss rifle for long-range engagements. Like Configuration A, the H variant derives from the same chassis philosophy of mounting outsized weaponry on a light frame, but the heavy lasers' increased damage output at short range gives pilots a more potent close-quarters option at the cost of reduced accuracy from the weapon type's inherent beam diffusion.

Alternate Configuration I employs a targeting computer to enhance the accuracy of its energy weapon suite, consisting of an ER PPC, ER medium laser, and ER small laser. Modular armor panels bolted onto the arms, legs, and side torsos increase survivability significantly, while an engine supercharger provides brief bursts of speed exceeding one hundred kilometers per hour. This configuration stands as a significant investment in advanced technology, creating an accurate, well-protected fire support platform that trades pod flexibility for focused lethality.

Alternate Configuration J carries a UAC/5 and Streak SRM-2 in the right arm, complemented by two ER medium lasers in the left arm. Six jump jets distributed across the legs and side torsos provide a one hundred eighty meter jump capability, making the Kit Fox J one of the more mobile configurations. Two tons of autocannon ammunition and one ton of Streak missiles ensure sustained combat endurance. The combination of jump mobility and mixed-range weaponry makes this configuration well-suited for the striker role, allowing pilots to exploit terrain while maintaining consistent firepower output.

Alternate Configuration K serves as a heavy striker, mounting an LB 10-X autocannon in the right arm and an improved heavy large laser in the left arm. Two tons of LB-X ammunition provide sustained fire with the option of cluster or slug rounds. The improved heavy laser delivers exceptional damage for a weapon of its class, though its bulk and heat generation demand careful shot discipline. This configuration excels at ambush engagements where the Kit Fox can deliver its considerable alpha strike before repositioning.

The Primary configuration balances long-range precision with close-quarters capability. An ER large laser and small pulse laser occupy the left arm, while the right arm mounts an LB 5-X autocannon with a ton of ammunition and a Streak SRM-4 launcher. This loadout allows MechWarriors to engage effectively at multiple range bands, with the LB-X's cluster munitions providing additional tactical options against lighter targets. The configuration represents the Kit Fox's core design philosophy of delivering versatile firepower from a light chassis.

Alternate Configuration R emphasizes sustained ballistic firepower through a Rotary AC/5 in the left arm, fed by two tons of ammunition. A Streak SRM-6 in the right arm provides close-range punch with a single ton of missiles. The rotary autocannon's variable rate of fire allows pilots to conserve ammunition during lighter engagements while unleashing devastating bursts against priority targets. The configuration's reliance on ammunition-dependent weapons makes extended operations a concern, but its raw damage output in short engagements is formidable for a light OmniMech.

Alternate Configuration S is purpose-built for urban warfare, mounting six jump jets that provide exceptional mobility through dense cityscapes. A large pulse laser serves as the primary weapon, supported by a medium pulse laser and small pulse laser for accurate fire at various ranges. A Streak SRM-4 launcher adds missile capability, while dual machine guns provide effective anti-infantry point defense. The all-pulse-laser energy weapon suite capitalizes on the close engagement ranges typical of urban combat, where the weapons' accuracy bonus compensates for the Kit Fox's relatively modest speed.

Alternate Configuration T is a Tiburon Khanate-era refresh designed primarily for scouting operations. An active probe in the right torso provides detection capability, while an engine supercharger grants brief speed increases for disengagement or pursuit. The left arm carries an ER large laser and ER medium laser for ranged engagements, while the right arm mounts a ProtoMech AC/4 with two tons of ammunition alongside a Streak SRM-4 with one ton of missiles. This configuration combines modern technology with the Kit Fox's proven scout-capable chassis to produce an effective reconnaissance platform for ilClan-era operations.

Alternate Configuration W is commonly employed as a training configuration by Clan Wolf, Clan Wolf-in-Exile, and Wolf's Dragoons. Armed with a pair of large pulse lasers as primary weapons and two medium pulse lasers for close-range work, the configuration mounts lower and hand actuators on the right arm. The all-energy loadout eliminates ammunition dependency, making the Kit Fox W well-suited for extended training exercises and garrison duty. The pulse laser suite also provides respectable combat capability, ensuring these training platforms remain viable battlefield assets when pressed into frontline service.

text.overview: The Kodiak II is an advanced, successful command ’Mech, though it never supplanted the original Kodiak as a close combat brawler. The Dominion has the infrastructure to produce both generations of the assault ’Mech at different facilities, and GKT debuted the newest iteration of the classic Kodiak in 3131. The Kodiak shows up whenever one of the Dominion’s big fire support ’Mechs needs something equally big to draw attention—and fire—away from it.
text.notableUnits: Star Captain Matthew Hall: Matthew Hall was an impressionable, young MechWarrior when he followed Isis Bekker and the 357th Assault Cluster to Vega. The Freeminder view on family proved too attractive in that faraway prefecture, and he soon made MechWarrior Emma his wife. Now a mature Star Captain, Hall leads from the front in his Kodiak while Emma provides tactical coordination from her Kodiak II. His Trinary has become known for its fraternity, even by Ghost Bear standards, where everyone including the technicians is considered a valued part of the family. :br::tab:Hall goes to great efforts to present his group of very public Freeminders in a positive light. The 357th suffered heavy losses taking Lambrecht in 3150. When the Cluster moved on to Dyev and found themselves facing only militia, Hall won the bid with his Trinary. The heavily outnumbered warriors ground their way through multiple battalions of militia, using the terrain to their advantage. With his techs maintaining a fast repair tempo, Hall cycled his ’Mechs in and out of battle, completing the operation without a single loss.

production.manufacturer: Bergan Industries - Alshain Weapons(formerly GK&T owned)

text.overview:
The Kodiak II is a hundred-ton assault BattleMech developed by the Ghost Bear Dominion, based upon the fourth variant of the original Kodiak. Entering production in 3095 at the Alshain Weapons facility, the Kodiak II was engineered to serve dual roles as both a powerful frontline assault 'Mech and a dedicated command platform. Where the original Kodiak excelled as a close-combat brawler, the Kodiak II reoriented the design toward long-range missile warfare and sophisticated command capabilities, reflecting the evolving needs of the Rasalhague Dominion's military doctrine.

The enhanced Garret L20 communications system features twelve extra multifunction displays and simultaneous audio and video channels, providing commanding officers with unparalleled battlefield awareness while remaining in the thick of combat. The design quickly became a favored mount for Star Colonels and other senior officers within the Ghost Bear touman, its combination of firepower, survivability, and command functionality proving ideal for leaders who direct Trinary-level and larger formations from the front lines.
text.capabilities:
The Kodiak II retains the hundred-ton mass and 400-rated extra-light engine of its predecessor, maintaining the same impressive sixty-four kilometer per hour top speed on an Alshain LXL Endo Steel chassis. The design fundamentally reoriented its combat philosophy from close-range brawling to long-range missile engagement. The primary armament consists of paired Type XX "Great Bow" LRM-20 launchers mounted in each arm, supplemented by a Type X "Short Bow" LRM-10 in the left torso, all guided by Artemis IV fire control systems for improved accuracy. A Clan Mk. XVII extended-range PPC in the right torso provides direct-fire long-range support.

For close-range defense, eight Series 1 extended-range small lasers are distributed across both arms, and all energy weapons feed through an integrated targeting computer for enhanced accuracy. The Kodiak II carries nineteen tons of Forging AD56 standard armor, providing robust protection. However, the RCA Instatrac targeting system has exhibited documented malfunctions when running near capacity, including false-positive missile lock readings and occasional failure-to-fire incidents. Alshain Weapons issued a service bulletin in 3105 to address these deficiencies, though a significant number of Kodiak IIs in the field have not received the update.
text.deployment: The most radical departure from the base Kodiak II, this variant focuses on overwhelming mid-to-short-range firepower and especially incorporates Inner Sphere weaponry, an unusual choice for a Dominion design. Each arm mounts a massive MRM-40 launcher with Apollo fire control system, delivering devastating salvos at medium engagement ranges. An LB 20-X autocannon spread between the right and center torso provides close-range lethality with both cluster and slug ammunition options. Like its predecessor, this variant employs the fragile XXL engine, and four tons of MRM ammunition are protected by CASE II in the left torso. The use of Inner Sphere missile technology has been linked to experiments within Omega Galaxy, where hybrid weapons configurations have been observed in an effort to surprise opponents accustomed to standard Clan armaments.
text.battleHistory:
The Kodiak II emerged in 3095 as the Rasalhague Dominion sought to modernize its assault 'Mech roster while preserving the legacy of the original Kodiak. Based specifically on the Kodiak 4 variant's weapons philosophy of combining long-range missile capability with close-range hitting power, the new design shifted the primary emphasis from pure close-combat brawling to long-range engagement and battlefield command. Produced at the Alshain Weapons facility (the same Alshain complex where the original Kodiak had been built for decades) the Kodiak II benefited from established manufacturing infrastructure and deep institutional knowledge of the chassis.

The design quickly proved its worth in combat. During a border skirmish on Jabuka in 3140, elements of Clan Jade Falcon's Fifty-third Battle Cluster engaged the Second Bear Regulars. The Kodiak II's sophisticated command capabilities proved essential as the engagement devolved into a running battle through rugged terrain surrounding Squaw Bay. When Jade Falcon artillery found its mark and engulfed the command Star, the Kodiak II weathered the bombardment better than its companions. Despite losing two 'Mechs to artillery fire during the approach, the surviving Star reached firing range and drove off the Falcon forces within minutes.

The Kodiak II 2 appeared in the early thirty-second century, introducing HarJel III self-repair technology and Streak LRM launchers at the cost of the more resilient XL engine. More recently, Kodiak IIs operating with Omega Galaxy have been observed with experimental hybrid loadouts incorporating Inner Sphere MRM launchers and Apollo fire control systems, marking an unusual willingness to adopt non-Clan weapons technology. The Kodiak II continues to serve as the preferred command assault platform of the Rasalhague Dominion, maintaining the proud lineage of the Ghost Bear's iconic totem design while adapting to the demands of a new era of warfare.

text.overview: Ramiel Bekker claims the Kontio was inspired by an encounter with a concealed ghost bear during hisClawing. The use of claws and stealth armor is as controversial as Bekker invoking the ghost bear’s hunting techniques when championing the concept for production. In any case, the Kontio caused a stir in the Rasalhague Dominion and even drew the attention of Wolf Khan Alaric Ward, who later claimed Bekker as a bondsman. With Clan Wolf as a source of steady demand, the Dominion could hold off difficult questions about its own doctrinal use of the Kontio and let customers perform combat testing for them.
text.capabilities: The Kontio is a clawed melee monstrosity that displays Bekker’s tactical preference for speed and positioning. Bekker himself proved the validity of the concept in a combat trial by impaling the opposing pilot with the Kontio’s claws, but the implicit dishonor in such a victory almost ended the project. The speed and efficiency he demonstrated forced reluctant consideration. Bergan Industries produced a single test run, before the Wolves created sudden demand. Bergan used its Capellan connection to source stealth armor and triple-strength myomer, and a growing number of Kontios have since appeared in the CCAF.:br::tab:The Kontio is becoming known as a pilot killer. It offers a poor death on the end of its claws. Enemy pilots either avoid Kontios or target them, for fear of a messy end.
text.battleHistory: When proving his new ’Mech, Ramiel Bekker requested an opponent with heavy head protection for safety. Star Captain Justine hoped to embarrass the ristar in her Savage Wolf. Bekker frustrated her with stealth, range, and terrain until she stopped moving to improve her aim. Bekker used the Kontio’s speed to stab the Savage Wolf in the back. Heat sink coolant dripping from its claw, Bekker broke for cover. The Kontio took heavy fire when the Savage Wolf whirled around. Unable to escape, Bekker smashed a claw into its cockpit. He backed away and demanded the exposed Justine yield. She refused and fired everything she had. Despite multiple system failures and the loss of an arm, Bekker managed to re-orient himself as the Savage Wolf charged. They slammed together, arms flailing wildly. The larger ’Mech slumped to the ground and Bekker’s Kontio stood tall, with Justine’s mangled remains impaled on its claw.:br::tab:For the freeborn Wolf Clusters raised from the Free Worlds League and Lyran Commonwealth, the Kontio has become a potent symbol of clawed predation. Cunning paintwork by Bergan to give the ursid Kontio a canid or feline appearance helps sell the image. Relatively rare and expensive for a garrison Cluster, Kontios are rewards for good service. While the Lyrans and League dare not threaten the Wolf Empire, the Falcons remain happy to raid. Attacks on Lamon, Sarpsborg, and Clinton have led to Kontios trying to chase down leaping Hierofalcons and Ion Sparrows. The clashes between inexperienced freeborn warriors on both sides resulted in messy affairs where ranges were short, and missed shots and physical confrontations were plentiful. More experienced Wolf warriors usually held back and scored easy kills when their enthusiastic comrades were finished.
text.notableUnits: Star Captain Evelyn Carrera: Few have done more to promote the Kontio in the Dominion than thenStar Commander Evelyn. The tactically skilled Evelyn suffered the embarrassment of having her Bear Cub shot from under her by the First Falcon Jaegers when the Eighteenth Battle Cluster retreated from La Grave. After failing to soothe her lust for revenge with her violin playing, she started hunting Falcon Jaegers under the guise of trialing for supplies. With her Star’s heavy ’Mechs forming a defensive redoubt, Evelyn would sally forth in her new Kontio and target Jaeger pilots in their cockpits. As tit-for-tat raids began to escalate, Galaxy Commander Hans Kabrinski called an end to these expeditions. Evelyn redirected her focus and used her unconventional tactics to blaze through her Trials of Position and Bloodright. Her hunger was finally sated, and she returned to her great work, a violin concerto.:br:Star Commander George: George Zhang was a street rat who descended into a life of crime on Gienah. Then Clan Wolf occupied the world. The opportunity to join the Wolf Touman was not only an honor, but a chance to stick it to the Lyran policemen who had made his life miserable. To the shock of all, George had sufficient aptitude piloting a ’Mech to pass his Trial of Position with two kills. George’s street smarts translated into instinctive evasive maneuvers and close quarter suckerpunches. As part of the Brown Keshik, George typically skulks around the edge of battle before pouncing on the unwary, regardless of size. A flurry of claws is usually the last thing his target sees.

text.overview: The Lancelot was originally designed as a heavy cavalry unit. Later it was touted to become the SLDF’s standard antiaircraft   ’Mech, although this was halted by the Amaris Crisis. The resurrection of its line on Luthien was made possible by the ’Mech being redesigned to share common parts with the Grand Dragon. ClanTech ER and pulse lasers provide the -09’s primary and secondary weapons, supported with a deadly plasma rifle. Much-strengthened armor improves its endurance. It is often paired with newer Grand Dragons, providing fire support as the Dragons close in.
text.notableUnits: Chu-i Knut Amano: Of Rasalhagian heritage, Amano’s grandparents escaped to the Combine following the Ghost Bear’s invitation into the Republic. Amano is stationed with the Seventh Legion of Vega on the Dominion border. He spends considerable effort funding anti-Bear sentiments in his off-duty time. Fragmentary Watch reports suggest his grandparents may have been part of Mimir. It is unlikely the ISF does not know about his activities, but as long as the secret police are focused on the Dragon’s enemies, they will likely turn a blind eye.:br::tab:Combat came to Shionoha in the early 3140s in the form of raids by the Ghost Bear’s 343rd Battle Cluster and Third Vega Regulars. Despite the mauling the Seventh received, the chu-i relished finally being able to face off against the Bears. The Third Regulars again raided in April 3150, catching the Seventh as they were preparing to rotate to the Federated Suns front. Forced into the field from their DropShips, the Seventh devastated the Regulars. Less than a quarter of the Third escaped. Reports suggest Amano may soon be promoted to tai-i, after gaining three kills in the close confines of the spaceport.

text.notes: Design Quirks: Exposed Actuators, Exposed Weapon Linkage (RAC/5), Poor Sealing, Easy to Maintain, Stable, Rumble Seat.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration B transforms the Linebacker into a dedicated sniper platform, built around a Gauss rifle that delivers devastating kinetic impacts at extreme range without generating waste heat. Three ER Medium Lasers and an ER Small Laser provide secondary firepower for closer engagements. The unusual placement of the Gauss rifle in the right torso has proven a nasty surprise for opponents expecting the weapon in an arm mount, as Inner Sphere MechWarriors unfamiliar with the configuration have learned to their cost that targeting the arms does not neutralize the Linebacker B's primary threat.

Alternate Configuration C serves as a versatile trooper loadout capable of engaging enemies at any range. An Ultra Autocannon/5 and ER Large Laser handle long-range engagements, while four ER Medium Lasers deliver concentrated energy damage at closer distances. The configuration emphasizes rear-arc defense with a rear-mounted ER Medium Laser, rear-mounted machine gun, and rear-mounted flamer, making it particularly effective in fluid engagements where enemies may attempt to exploit the Linebacker's flanks during running battles. A second forward-mounted machine gun provides additional anti-infantry capability.

Alternate Configuration D was designed for close-quarters combat, mounting four Streak SRM-6 launchers that deliver an overwhelming missile barrage at short range with near-perfect accuracy. Two ER Medium Lasers and a rear-mounted ER Small Laser supplement the missile systems. This configuration fully exploits the Linebacker's speed advantage, closing rapidly to brawling range where the Streak launchers can inflict maximum damage. The configuration's effectiveness is limited by its ammunition dependency, as its three bins can be exhausted during prolonged engagements, requiring the MechWarrior to manage fire discipline carefully.

Alternate Configuration E leverages the flexibility of Advanced Tactical Missile technology, mounting a pair of ATM-6 launchers with magazine capacity for multiple ammunition types. An ER Large Laser provides consistent direct fire support, while a Light Active Probe enhances the configuration's reconnaissance capability. The ATM launchers allow MechWarriors to select ammunition optimized for the engagement range, from extended-range bombardment to devastating short-range high-explosive salvos, making this configuration exceptionally adaptable to changing battlefield conditions.

Alternate Configuration G is a Dark Age-era design that pushes the Linebacker's speed envelope with an engine Supercharger capable of propelling the OmniMech to bursts of one hundred and twenty kilometers per hour. Its primary armament consists of paired Improved Heavy Large Lasers linked to a Targeting Computer for enhanced accuracy, delivering tremendous damage at medium range. A pair of Improved One-Shot Streak SRM-2 launchers provide supplementary close-range firepower. The combination of extreme speed and precise, heavy-hitting weaponry makes this configuration ideal for slashing attacks against high-value targets, though the Supercharger carries inherent mechanical risk during sustained use.

Alternate Configuration H introduces jump capability to the Linebacker chassis, mounting six jump jets that allow the OmniMech to cover up to one hundred and eighty meters in a single bound. Paired Heavy Large Lasers serve as the primary armament, delivering massive damage at medium range. Two ER Medium Lasers and an ER Small Laser provide supporting firepower, with an additional double heat sink helping to manage the considerable thermal output. The addition of jump jets transforms the Linebacker's tactical profile, enabling it to exploit terrain features and execute flanking maneuvers that would be impossible for the ground-bound standard chassis.

The primary configuration emphasizes long-range engagement, mounting a pair of ER PPCs capable of delivering punishing fire at extreme distances. An LRM-5 launcher supplements the energy weapons with indirect fire capability, while a Streak SRM-4 provides efficient close-range defense and a rear-mounted ER Small Laser deters pursuit. This loadout is optimized for the Linebacker's intended role as a fast striker, allowing MechWarriors to exploit the OmniMech's speed to maintain favorable engagement ranges while delivering concentrated firepower against targets of opportunity.

Alternate Configuration T is a Tiburon Khanate refresh of the Linebacker platform, incorporating modern weapon systems to update the design for the ilClan era. Twin Plasma Cannons serve as the primary armament, offering versatile damage combined with the ability to dramatically increase an opponent's heat burden. A Streak SRM-4 and Streak LRM-5 provide supplementary missile fire, while a rear-mounted flamer and forward-mounted Active Probe round out the electronics suite. This configuration is optimized for skirmishing engagements where the plasma weapons' heat-transfer properties can degrade enemy combat effectiveness over sustained exchanges.

text.overview:
The Lineholder was introduced in 3058 as the first BattleMech design produced by Kressly Warworks on Epsilon Eridani. Created using a set of "Common Sense Design" guidelines, the fifty-five-ton 'Mech was developed by a Kressly think tank to meet self-imposed standards for speed, heat management, weapons-to-heat-sink ratios, and damage bracket projections. The result is a medium-weight platform that balances firepower, protection, and mobility at a price point attractive to small commands, minor nobles, and garrison forces throughout the Chaos March.

In its first year of production, the Lineholder achieved remarkable commercial success compared to other designs in its weight class, rapidly becoming the garrison machine of choice for factions able to afford newly manufactured BattleMechs. The design's affordable price point and reliance on easy-to-source components have kept it in production across multiple political upheavals, a sign of the enduring appeal of Kressly's common-sense engineering philosophy.
text.capabilities:
The Lineholder is built around a philosophy of reliability and simplicity. A standard Kressly GRF1A-MDX chassis carries a Core Tek 275 fusion engine, giving the 'Mech a top speed of 86 kilometers per hour, sufficient to keep pace with all but the fastest light and medium designs. Ten tons of Kressly Stoneskin 30M armor provide above-average protection for its weight class, reinforcing the 'Mech's intended role as a dependable workhorse rather than a specialized combatant.

The Lineholder's weapons suite emphasizes versatility across engagement ranges. A pair of LongFire V LRM-5 launchers provide long-range fire support and limited indirect capability, while a BlazeFire Systems large laser delivers accurate damage at medium ranges. Four Intek medium lasers round out the arsenal, creating a formidable close-range deterrent. Fourteen heat sinks manage the thermal load effectively, allowing sustained fire in all but the most prolonged engagements.

The design's reliance on proven, off-the-shelf components is both its greatest strength and its principal limitation. While the Lineholder is remarkably easy to maintain and repair (a quality reinforced by its widely recognized Easy to Maintain design quirk) it lacks the specialized edge of more expensive competitors. Many commands assign the Lineholder as the damage dealer in a medium attack lance or as the quick-response element of a heavier assault company, roles that play to its combination of speed, firepower, and endurance.
text.deployment: Introduced in the early 3130s under Republic of the Sphere production, this variant stands as a significant departure from earlier Lineholder designs. It replaces all previous weaponry with a plasma rifle for primary firepower, supported by MML-5 launchers providing flexible missile capability and medium pulse lasers for close defense. The addition of a C3 emergency master computer made this variant particularly popular in command lances, allowing it to serve as a network coordination node while maintaining respectable combat capability. The design reflects the Republic's emphasis on networked warfare doctrine and multi-role flexibility.
text.battleHistory:
The Lineholder emerged in 3058 from Kressly Warworks, an independent manufacturer operating on Epsilon Eridani in the contested Chaos March. Kressly's think tank developed the design using their "Common Sense Design" guidelines, a set of self-imposed engineering principles governing speed, thermal management, and weapons effectiveness. The result was a medium BattleMech that offered solid performance at a highly competitive price, a combination that proved irresistible to the minor factions, garrison commands, and independent units that formed the bulk of Kressly's target market.

The Lineholder's commercial success in its first years of production was remarkable by any standard for a new design. Its affordable price point and reliance on common, easy-to-source components made it the garrison machine of choice across the Chaos March, and demand quickly spread to the Federated Suns, the Word of Blake, and even Periphery states such as the Circinus Federation. This early success encouraged Kressly to invest in variant development, producing upgraded models targeting higher-paying customers.

The relationship between Kressly Warworks and the Word of Blake proved particularly significant. When the Blakists gained control of Epsilon Eridani during the late Civil War era, Kressly came under Word of Blake ownership, resulting in the development of the advanced KW2-LHW variant with integrated C3i networking. Simultaneously, Kressly produced the Linebreaker variant exclusively for the Federated Suns, until production was abruptly suspended following the dissolution of the second Star League, apparently as Blakist retaliation for the Federated Suns' no-confidence vote.

During the Jihad, Kressly Warworks continued operations under Word of Blake control, producing the LHW and base Lineholder variants for Blakist forces. Following the liberation of Epsilon Eridani and the establishment of the Republic of the Sphere, the factory transitioned to Republic oversight, resuming broader production including the previously suspended Linebreaker. The Republic era also saw the introduction of the KW2-LH10, a thoroughly modernized variant incorporating plasma weaponry and C3 emergency master technology that proved popular in command lances.

With the collapse of the Republic and the rise of the ilClan era, Epsilon Eridani passed to Capellan Confederation control, and Kressly Warworks continues to produce the Lineholder under its latest owners, proof of the enduring commercial viability of a design built from the start on principles of affordability, simplicity, and common sense.
